MCP Console lets your agent run R, Python, and SQL in a persistent session.
It can load data once, inspect results, refine plots, read help, and debug code with objects and models still in memory.

Code runs in an [OS-level sandbox](SANDBOX.md) by default.
Console prepares environments and packages automatically; no Console configuration file is required.

[Get started](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [User guides](README.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

## An interactive workbench for agents

REPLs let people explore a question one step at a time: run code, inspect the result, and decide what to try next.
Console gives agents those same interactive affordances in an environment tailored to how they work.

During an analysis, the agent can load a dataset, fit a model, and plot the residuals.
A follow-up question can use the same data and model rather than repeat the setup.

The agent can read help, inspect intermediate results, pause in a debugger, and continue after an interruption.
Long computations can keep running between calls.
Previews keep long output out of the model's context, while [recordings](RECORDING.md) retain logs and plots for later inspection.

## Use one language or combine them {#one-workspace-three-languages}

Console embeds R, Python, and DuckDB in one process.
[Reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/) connects R and Python, and [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) can query in-memory data frames as SQL views.
The agent can choose the language that fits each step, reusing live data and models without exporting and reloading intermediate files.

R and Python can each run without the other.

See [Working with R, Python, and SQL](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md) for examples, database connections, and plots.

## Build on Console

Build LLM applications on Console's persistent runtime.
Replace the complete [tool description and instructions](TOOL_CONFIGURATION.md#tool-descriptions-and-parameters), choose which language interfaces and parameters the model can use, and [preconfigure the runtime](CONFIGURATION.md).
Set [sandbox permissions](SANDBOX_CONFIGURATION.md) to control access to files and networks.

For example, build a data chat with only SQL and a selected database connection, or a reporting assistant with a prepared R or Python environment.

Console works with MCP-compatible clients such as Codex and Claude Code and does not depend on a particular model provider.
To connect from your own application, see [Client integration](CLIENTS.md).

## Choose how packages are prepared {#environment-setup}

By default, Console prepares packages for the session and reuses cached installations.
The agent can request additional packages as it works.

You can instead [select an existing Python environment](CONFIGURATION.md#python-environment-selection) or choose when Console may prepare dependencies.
See [Packages and environments](REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Where Console fits

- **Unattended analysis:** run long analyses with limits on filesystem writes and network access.
- **Model evaluations:** evaluate how an agent explores data, checks its work, and responds to results.
- **Conversational analysis:** discuss questions and results while the agent works in its own session.
- **Large datasets:** keep data and intermediate results in memory for follow-up questions.
- **Debugging and package development:** pause execution and inspect live objects where a failure occurs.

## Status and trust

Console is a **development preview** for macOS, Linux, and Windows x64.
Run it on the same host as the MCP client.

Without [client permission inheritance](SANDBOX_CONFIGURATION.md#inherit-permissions-from-codex) or a configured profile, Console defaults to `read_only`: it restricts network access and filesystem writes but places no restrictions on filesystem reads.
You can select a different profile or customize a profile by creating a [`.agents/console/config.yaml` file](CONFIGURATION.md) or supplying configuration arguments on the command line.
Customizations let you manage network access through a [built-in proxy](SANDBOX_CONFIGURATION.md#proxy-modes-and-destinations) with domain allowlists or denylists, allow filesystem writes to specific paths, and block filesystem reads from selected paths.

Project configuration is trusted input and may widen permissions.
Dependency preparation has a separate policy.

[Recordings](RECORDING.md) capture input and output from an MCP Console session.
They are unredacted, so check for secrets before sharing session files.
For example, a recording may include a secret printed by code the agent ran.
